types.name: FAINoiseCell
types.doc:
FAINoiseMap — where it has been loud lately, as the level's acoustics carry
it. Every sound and scan the perception system files is spread over a grid
of cells around it, each cell receiving what the propagation law lets
through to its centre (walls, doors and distance), and the whole map fades
with a half-life. The director reads it to know which player is making the
noise and where to send what is hunting them; a perceiver could sample it to
drift toward a din it never heard as a single event.

The map is horizontal: a cell is keyed by X and Z, its height is the height
of the loudest noise that landed in it, so a corridor above a corridor still
keeps the noise on the floor it happened on.

types.name: FAIStimulus
types.doc:
FAIStimulusBus — everything the AI can sense, filed by where it is.

Gameplay emits stimuli (a sound, a flare seen, a scan pulse, a hit) with a
position, a strength and a type; perceivers ask the bus for what lies around
them instead of walking every actor and every event in the world. Both
halves are indexed by the same 8 m sector key the point-cloud renderer
chunks by (FPointCloudSector) — one spatial hash for the scan the players
see and the stimuli the creatures sense, so a later change to the chunk size
moves both together or neither.

Events live in a fixed ring with a timestamp and a lifetime, and every event
has a rising id. A perceiver remembers the last id it consumed, so one that
only ticks every fourth frame (significance stagger) still hears the
gunshot that happened between its ticks, and none hears the same one twice.
When the ring is full the oldest event is overwritten and counted.

Presence — where the perceivable targets are this frame — is rebuilt by the
perception system each tick and queried the same way for sight and touch.

types.name: EBTFlowAbortMode
types.doc:
Observer abort modes (UE5 EBTFlowAbortMode). Self is implicit on every gate
decorator here — the condition is re-evaluated on each tick, so a running
subtree is dropped the moment it stops holding. LowerPriority/Both make the
enclosing Selector re-check this gate while a lower-priority sibling runs and
switch back to it the moment the condition passes again. A gate with any
mode other than None also registers its blackboard keys as observed, so a
change to one of them ticks a throttled tree at once.

members.name: Execute
members.doc:
Enter-on-fresh + Tick + reset-on-terminal. A node entered last tick that
returned Running is NOT re-entered (OnEnter skipped) so it can resume.

members.name: AbortIfRunning
members.doc:
Cancels an abandoned Running subtree: aborts the running children first,
then runs OnAbort and clears the running flag, so the next Execute is a
fresh entry (OnEnter runs, per-entry state resets). A node that is not
running is left alone. Call it wherever a branch stops being ticked —
a gate decorator that starts failing, a composite restarting from 0, a
parallel whose main task finished.

members.name: GetAbortMode
members.doc:
Observer contract, honoured by the enclosing Selector. A gate decorator
reports the mode it was authored with and whether its condition passes
right now; everything else opts out.

members.name: CollectObservedKeys
members.doc:
Blackboard keys whose change can flip this node's condition. A tree
collects them from every node with an abort mode, so a throttled tree
wakes the frame one of them changes (UE's blackboard observers) instead
of finding out on its next scheduled tick.

members.doc:

the Vec3 in blackboard `destKey`. Running until within `acceptance` (or the
agent reports arrived), then Success; Failure if there's no pawn/agent.
acceptance <= 0 uses the agent's stoppingDistance.

members.name: FindCover
members.signature: static NodePtr FindCover(FName threatKey, float maxDistance = 25.0f)
members.doc:
Cover tasks (implemented in CoverSystem.cpp, backed by FCoverSystem).
FindCover reads the threat position from `threatKey`, reserves the best
point and writes its position to "CoverPosition" + id to "CoverPointId".
MoveToCover drives the NavAgent toward the reserved point. InCover is a
condition: reserved + not flanked + within `acceptance`. LeaveCover
releases the reservation.

members.name: MeleeAttack
members.signature: static NodePtr MeleeAttack(FName targetKey, float range = 0.0f, float cooldown = 0.0f)
members.doc:
Melee task (implemented in MeleeSystem.cpp, backed by FMeleeSystem).
Reads the target actor from blackboard `targetKey`, fails when it is
missing or beyond range (0 = the equipped weapon's range), otherwise faces
it, requests an attack and stays Running until the swing resolves, then
Success. After a completed swing the node reports Failure for `cooldown`
seconds.

types.name: NavAgentComponent
types.doc:
An entity that moves itself toward a destination using the navigation
system. The agent's TransformComponent.position is steered each tick;
it doesn't interact with physics rigid bodies directly (that's a
separate "physics-driven nav agent" pattern, deferred).

Phase-1 movement: straight-line steering at `speed` m/s. Once Recast is
vendored the system replaces this with a Detour-pathed sequence of
waypoints + smooth corner following + dynamic avoidance. The component
surface stays the same — gameplay code that just calls SetDestination
won't need to change when the upgrade lands.

types.name: NavAgentSystem
types.doc:
Steers every NavAgentComponent toward its destination each frame.

Three operating modes, picked automatically based on what's available:

1. NavMesh + dtCrowd (preferred): one dtCrowd manages every agent.
Avoidance, anticipation, and separation are handled by Detour.
Per-tick we feed destinations in and read back positions —
agents push around each other instead of overlapping.

2. NavMesh, no crowd (initialization failure path): fall back to
single-agent Detour findPath + findStraightPath path-follow.
No agent-to-agent avoidance.

3. No NavMesh: straight-line steering at agent.speed, ignoring
everything. Same behavior the Scope-A skeleton had — keeps the
system functional in unbaked scenes.

types.name: NavAgentSystem::EPathRequestState
types.doc:
Gameplay path requests answered over later frames (UE's
FindPathAsync). Each Update spends at most nav.PathQueryBudget
Detour search iterations on the queue through a sliced search
(initSlicedFindPath / updateSlicedFindPath) on a query object of its
own, highest priority first and FIFO within a priority, so a burst of
requests costs a bounded slice of a frame instead of one synchronous
findPath per caller. A request that runs out of budget resumes on the
next frame where it stopped. A nav mesh swap restarts the request in
flight; a partial rebake that invalidates its polygons fails it.

types.name: NavMeshAsset
types.doc:
Baked navigation mesh. Owns:
- The serialized Detour blob (m_blob) — what gets written to disk and
re-loaded on scene open.
- A live dtNavMesh built from that blob (m_navMesh) — what queries run
against.
- A shared dtNavMeshQuery handle wrapping the nav mesh (m_query).
- Debug-viz triangles (m_triangles) for editor overlay.

Memory ownership: the blob bytes are also passed to dtNavMesh::init
(DT_TILE_FREE_DATA), so on Unload Detour frees them — we must NOT free
m_blob ourselves once it's been handed off. The pre-handoff "rejected"
path (init failure) does free.

types.name: NavMeshBuilder
types.doc:
Runs the Recast bake pipeline against a scene. Walks every entity with
TransformComponent + MeshRendererComponent, transforms the CPU-side mesh
data to world space, feeds Recast, and produces a dtNavMesh ready to stuff
into a NavMeshAsset.

Solo (single-tile) mode is the default and stays fast for indoor / mid-size
scenes. Set NavMeshBakeSettings::tiled to partition the scene bounds into a
grid of tileSize² chunks and bake each independently — the composed dtNavMesh
scales to open worlds and stays under Detour's per-tile poly cap. Both paths
report the actual polygon and tile counts walked from the built mesh.

Fold of every terrain's paint and build state at snapshot time. The

types.name: NavMeshBuilder::TileBatch
types.doc:
Runtime rebuild by change: tiles are baked on a worker into a batch
without touching the live mesh, and ApplyTileBatch swaps them in on the
game thread, where queries run. A batch that is never applied frees its

types.name: NavMeshObstacleSystem
types.doc:
Per-frame sync between NavMeshObstacleComponent entities and the
scene's dtTileCache. When a baked nav mesh has dynamicObstacles
enabled, this system:

- Adds an obstacle to the cache the first time it sees a component
(or first time it sees one whose registered flag is false).
- Re-adds (remove + add — dtTileCache has no "move") when the host
entity teleported more than `kObstacleMoveEpsilon` from where
the obstacle was last anchored.
- Removes when the component is disabled or the entity is gone.
- Calls dtTileCache::update(dt, navMesh) once per frame so pending
adds/removes apply incrementally without blocking the main thread.

With no nav mesh or with dynamicObstacles=false, the system early-
outs every tick — leaving NavMeshObstacleComponents inert.

types.name: NavMeshRebuildSystem
types.doc:
Rebuilds a tiled navmesh by change at runtime (UE's dynamic generation with
dirty areas). Every frame it notices nav-relevant geometry that moved,
appeared or disappeared — mesh renderers that are not simulated physics
bodies, compared by their transform's world version and mesh — and records
the old and new bounds as dirty. MarkDirty takes areas from gameplay
directly (a door, a destruction chunk, a deployable). Once the dirty set
has been quiet for nav.Rebuild.SettleTime seconds (or has waited
nav.Rebuild.MaxDelay), the touched tiles of every agent type's mesh are
baked on a worker, at most nav.Rebuild.MaxTiles per pass, and swapped in on
the game thread. Solo meshes and tile-cache meshes are left alone: the first
has no tiles to swap, the second already re-cuts itself through dynamic
obstacles.

types.name: SmartObjectComponent
types.doc:
A world object an agent can claim and use — a bench, a vending machine, a
window to look out of (UE5 SmartObjects). The object advertises an activity
and N slots laid out along its local X axis; an agent claims one slot, walks
to it, uses it for Use Duration and releases it, after which the slot rests
for Cooldown. Claims are exclusive, so two agents never sit on one seat.

members.name: activity
members.doc:
What using this object means ("Sit", "Inspect", "Hide"). Queries filter
on it; empty matches only an empty query.

members.name: slotSpacing
members.doc: Distance between neighbouring slots along the object's local X.

members.name: slotOffset
members.doc: Where a user stands, in the object's local space, before slot spacing.

members.name: claimants
members.doc:
Per slot: the claiming agent (INVALID_ENTITY = free) and the seconds
left before a released slot can be claimed again.
